pages.title: This / that / these / those
rules: This and that are for ONE thing; these and those are for MANY.
This / these = near me. That / those = far from me.
Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
examples: O que é aquilo? É um relógio.

pages.title: The sound /ɪ/ in this
pages.tip: A short, relaxed 'i', like in 'this' and 'it'. Do not make it long like /iː/ in 'these'. Compare: this /ðɪs/ – these /ðiːz/.

pages.head: The new classroom
text: Mia's classroom is on the first floor. There is a big board on the wall and a clock above the door. There are twelve desks, twelve chairs and four windows.

On Mia's desk there are books, pens and pencils. Zoe has a green bag. Paul has a blue bag. "What's this?" asks Zoe, pointing at a small box. "It's a pencil case," says Mia. "And what's that?" asks Paul, pointing at the clock. "That's a clock. It's nine o'clock. Time for class!"
The students sit down and open their notebooks. Mia writes a word on the board: WELCOME.
tf: There are twelve desks in the classroom.
Mia writes WELCOME on the board.

pages.title: Classroom: fact file
text: In English-speaking schools, students often have a 'locker' to keep their things.
In the UK, 'rubber' is an eraser. In the USA, 'rubber' means something different, so say 'eraser'!
'Pencil case' (UK) and 'pencil box' (USA) are small containers for pens and pencils.
